what: vLLM 0.32.0 serving gpt-oss-20b (openai/gpt-oss-20b safetensors, MXFP4), --enforce-eager --max-model-len 3072, greedy chat completions with top-20 logprobs for 48 prompts (max 200 tokens), sent one at a time and then 16 at once; experiments/vllm_determinism.py. Compared token by token and value by value (positions before any divergence).

default_mode.rtx4090_norway: 1-at-a-time vs 16-at-onc: 45/48 replies diverge; values differ at 4,281/4,334 positions before divergence

batch_invariant_mode (VLLM_BATCH_INVARIA.across the identical group: 0/48 replies diverge, 0/9,493 positions differ, both modes (every pair)
batch_invariant_mode (VLLM_BATCH_INVARIA.H100 PCIe: not batch-invariant on itself (3/48 replies diverge, 384/9,426 positions differ between 1-at-a-time and 16-at-once); differs from the group on 44-45/48 replies
batch_invariant_mode (VLLM_BATCH_INVARIA.RTX 5090: batch-invariant on itself (0/48 replies diverge, 0/9,517 positions differ) but its own group: differs from the Ampere/Ada group and from the H100 on 46/48 replies

notes: Ampere and Ada take vLLM's Triton batch-invariant path, Hopper a cuBLAS path (vLLM source, per the research summary in docs/soundness.md); the H100 leak was not traced. Same vLLM, torch and model on every machine; drivers 580-610.

one_pass_referee (prompt_logprobs).what: a referee in batch-invariant mode scoring prompt+reply in one prefill (prompt_logprobs=20) vs the provider's token-by-token logprobs (experiments/vllm_onepass_referee.py)
one_pass_referee (prompt_logprobs).home RTX 4090 decode vs RTX 3090 prefill: top-20 differs at 9,493/9,493 positions; chosen-token logprob at 9,174
one_pass_referee (prompt_logprobs).same RTX 3090, its own decode vs its own: prompt identical (71 tokens); positions 0-2 agree up to tail rounding, position 3 differs by >5 nats (decode: token 976 at -0.78, chosen; prefill: 976 at -6.06, another token on top)
one_pass_referee (prompt_logprobs).conclusion: for gpt-oss in vLLM 0.32 the prefill path does not reproduce decode even on one machine, so the exact tier needs token-by-token replay (which is bit-identical across Ampere/Ada); not traced (gpt-oss sliding-window/sink attention in prefill is a guess)

accuracy_of_vllm_decode.what: the 48 replies the user's RTX 4090 generated with vLLM 0.32 (batch-invariant mode, eager) with their returned top-20 logprobs, scored on the same tokens by Hugging Face transformers in BF16 (A6000) and by llama.cpp (lv-engine, RTX 4090) one pass and token by token; experiments/path_noise.py compare
accuracy_of_vllm_decode.spot_check: reply position 3 of 'Name three colors.': vLLM decode token 976 at -0.78 (chosen greedily); vLLM prefill -6.14; llama.cpp one pass -6.37; llama.cpp step not in its top 3; also seen without batch-invariant mode
accuracy_of_vllm_decode.note: vLLM's own prefill (prompt_logprobs) sided with llama.cpp in the spot check. Kernel path on Ada: Marlin MXFP4 MoE, TRITON_ATTN; cause not traced. The Ampere/Ada machines that agree bit for bit agree on this less accurate decode: reproducible is not the same as accurate. OpenRouter gpt-oss-20b endpoints audited earlier (likely Hopper/Blackwell) were not affected.
